decisions.essenceRationale: Every customer engagement begins here: the platform's agents draft each design artifact inside the opinionated design system while the customer remains architect-of-record through review — the guardrailed alternative to open-ended agentic coding that is the platform's stated differentiator (objective 2). Whatever the artifact set or drafting tooling becomes, a business that delivers predictably-engineered software must always carry the customer's idea through a supervised design; remove this and the platform is a code generator, not a delivery business.

Apply price model -> compute build-cost ceiling

Revoke within grace window?
Revoke the commitment; await a new decision
Reject all options with feedback; return to project design

decisions.essenceRationale: Predictable delivery is the founding promise (objective 1): no construction begins until the customer has chosen among options with explicit duration, cost, and risk — each carrying a traceable operating-cost forecast (objective 5). Every customer on every project makes this informed commitment; the option mechanics may evolve, but a business selling predictability without the commitment decision is a contradiction.

Trigger scope-change replan

decisions.essenceRationale: This is where the delivery promise is redeemed: the agents the platform orchestrates perform the construction work activity-by-activity against the committed plan, inside generated guardrails, so a customer with no engineering staff still receives predictably-engineered software (objective 4). Venues, agents, and code generation will all churn, but orchestrated construction of the customer's system is what the business does — the mission's 'the platform orchestrates; it does not hand-author code' made operational.

nodes.label: Operated system in flight

No change needed?

decisions.essenceRationale: The vision ends 'delivers and operates it on the customer's behalf': operation is where the platform absorbs the genuinely hard work — running systems in production, scaling, load and cost projection — so the customer never becomes an operations engineer (objective 10). It is shared by every customer who hosts with the platform and it seats the operations-first revenue model (objective 3); infrastructure will change, operated-on-their-behalf will not.

decisions.essenceRationale: The platform's commercial engine is a usage-based fee for operating delivered systems on the customer's behalf — objective 3 makes this the initial and central revenue model, with cost transparency at every commitment (objective 5). Rates, meters, and future revenue lines will shift, but converting operated usage into revenue is the transaction the business exists to make; without it there is no business, only a tool.

decisions.rejectionReason: Question-type review comments (ratified 2026-07-05): a reviewer asks the PM or the architect for clarification without sending the draft back - a permutation of the Drive System Design review gate over the human-collaboration area of volatility. Open questions warn at approve but never gate it; a committed artifact seeds a question-only thread on main. No redraft and no orchestration of its own.

useCase.name: Send Back Change Requests for a Redraft

nodes.label: Reviewer anchors change-request comments to locations in the staged draft

decisions.rejectionReason: Change-request review comments: the reviewer's send-back with anchored, approve-gating comments that drive a redraft - the rejection permutation of the Drive System Design review gate. Feedback is retained in the durable thread on the session branch and each comment is answered by the redraft; same session, same ledger, no business behaviour beyond the core review loop.
